context: Sho-young loses something at school; calls Yumiko in tears.
purpose: Child seeking comfort over small loss.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おばあちゃん、宝物、失くした!
lines.style: Small, wavering voice on the opening. Urgent but not panicked — the distress of a six-year-old who's lost something that matters. Quiet catch in the throat at 'lost.' Seeking comfort, not performing sadness.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.style: Immediate, attentive lean-in. Warmth without fussing. The tone that says: I'm listening and this matters because you say it does. Soft, unhurried.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お父さんに、もらった鉛筆。
lines.style: Quiet, careful words. The voice of a child who knows the loss isn't really about the pencil. Slight tremor on 'Dad.' Pauses between phrases — not rushing, just gathering himself.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.style: Recognition, not repetition. Steady and even. The voice that mirrors his feeling back to him so he knows he's been understood. No rush to fix or console.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Soft acknowledgment of his own pain. Small voice, but real. Not asking permission to feel this way — stating it. Slight trailing-off, like he's surprised by his own honesty.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.style: Gentle shift — from comfort to action. Warm, steady, solution-oriented. The invitation of presence, not pity. Like she's saying: you're not alone in this.
